To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
blockade of the kinnin system did not alter basal blood pressure or potentiate the development of hypertension in rats given a high salt diet or a subpressor dose of angiotension II.
blockade of kinins did not potentiate hypertension induced by angiotensin, salt, and deoxycorticosteroids but did abolish the antihypersensitive effect of ramipril in DOCA-saline hypertension.

the kallikerein-kinin-gen-kinin system does not participate in the regulation of basal blood pressure and does not play a role in the development of hypertension in rats given angiotensin-II, a high salt intake or deoxycorticosteron-salt.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the kallikein-kinin-kinin (KKK) system in the regulation of BP.
the role of the kallikein-kinin-system in the regulation of blood pressure and in the development of hypertension.
the effect of the kallurein-kinin-kinin on blood pressure in rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the kallikerein-kinin-kinin-system does not participate in the development of hypertension in rats, but may play a minor role in the antinatriuretic effect of angiotensis II.
endogenous kinin does not participate in the development of hypertension in this experimental model.
the kallikerein-kinin-system plays a minor or no role in the development of hypertension in rats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the kallikerein-kinin-gen-kinin system has a very important physiological role in the maintenance of blood pressure and the development of hypertension, but it does not have a significant role in the development of hypertension in rats given chronic subpressor or nonpressor doses of Ang II or a high salt diet.
endogenous bradykinin is not involved in the maintenance of blood pressure and in hypertension induced by angiotensin, salt, or aldosterone.
the kallikren-kinin system has no effect on blood pressure in rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the kallikren-kinin system does not play an essential role in blood pressure regulation in rats, at least under conditions in which the system is intact.
the kallikirein-kinin pathway does not seem to play a role in hypertension.
kinins are not important in the maintenance of blood pressure in rats and that they do not play a role in the pathogenesis of hypertension induced by angiotensin, salt, or DOCA.
